raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through like the farmer I am.

---

It's spring already, wheat's been in the ground since October. Me and the wife, we've been working these 6 mu for thirty years now. Kids moved to the city long ago, they send a little money sometimes but we mostly get by on what this land gives us. Two old people, 6 mu, wheat and corn every year like always. That's how it goes.

**About the wheat** — I put it in on October 8th or so last fall, same as every year. I used my own saved seed mostly, got a bit more from my cousin who farms over in the next village. No sense buying new seed every year when the old variety does fine. Before planting I hired the neighbor's tiller man to turn the soil, 30 yuan per mu, and I spread about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu (that 15-15-15 stuff from the town shop) — threw it on by hand and the tiller worked it in. Watered once before the ground froze.

Now the wheat's been jointing. I already gave it one watering back in early April when I saw the topsoil drying out — well pumping isn't cheap, about 15 yuan per mu each time with the electric meter, so I don't do it more than I have to. At jointing I'll topdress urea, maybe 15 kg per mu — that's what Lao Zhang down the road does and his wheat always looks good. If the leaves look a bit yellow after that I'll add a handful more here and there, but I try not to waste it. Sprayed the weeds once already, one little bottle of 2,4-D mixed in the backpack sprayer, does the whole field. Another watering before it heads out in May, then let it ripen. I'm hoping for 450 kg per mu, got 460 last year so it should be close.

**Combine comes early June** to cut the wheat, 45 yuan per mu, hauls the grain to the edge. Then I've got maybe five, six days to get the maize in before the window closes.

**About the corn** — I don't plow after wheat, no time, no need. I use the little hand planter (borrowed from my nephew) and push it right through the stubble. Hybrid seed from the village shop, about 30 yuan per mu — the Zhengdan variety most people around here use. I drop compound fertilizer at planting, another bag per mu basically, then when it's about knee-high I topdress urea, another 15 kg or so. If July is dry I'll irrigate once, otherwise I let the rain do it. Last summer I didn't water it at all, the rain came at the right time. Got 520 kg per mu.

If I see worms at tasseling I'll spray once — cheap bottle from the shop, does the whole field in a morning. Don't bother otherwise.

**Money-wise** — inputs for the year run me somewhere around 3,300 yuan for the 6 mu all told. We eat maybe 200 kg of wheat ourselves, sell the rest. The corn mostly sells, goes to the feed dealer who comes around in October. Not much left after everything, but it's enough for two old people.
